record.question:
A legacy application runs on a supported EBS-backed EC2 instance. Licensing and external allowlists depend on its instance ID, private IPv4 address, and existing auto-assigned public IPv4 address. Those identifiers cannot change during recovery. The application can restart from its EBS data after a reboot. The team wants an AWS-managed response to an underlying host failure with configurable alarm thresholds and notifications.

Which solution best meets these requirements?

options.text: Associate a new Elastic IP address and automate stopping and starting the instance when its system status check fails.
Use Systems Manager Patch Manager to reinstall operating-system updates after any failed status check.
Create a CloudWatch alarm that reboots the instance when StatusCheckFailed_System indicates a failure.
Create a CloudWatch alarm on StatusCheckFailed_System with an EC2 recover action and the required SNS notifications.

explanation.text:
<<4>> is correct. CloudWatch action based recovery attempts to move a supported instance away from impaired underlying infrastructure while retaining its instance ID, addresses, and attached EBS volumes. The alarm supplies the requested threshold and notification controls.

<<1>> can be automated, but assigning a new Elastic IP replaces the existing public address. A stop/start without an Elastic IP also changes an auto-assigned public IPv4 address.

<<2>> addresses guest operating-system maintenance, not recovery from a failed host.

<<3>> reboots the guest on its current host and does not provide the recover action's host-relocation behavior.

Recovery resembles an unplanned reboot: RAM state is lost, and the application must restart safely. Success depends on supported configuration and available capacity. This is single-instance recovery, not an application architecture that survives an Availability Zone outage without interruption.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [EC2 automatic instance recovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-recover.html). [CloudWatch recover actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/cloudwatch-recovery.html).

diagram_alt: A recovery table separates preserved identity and persistent storage from replaced infrastructure and lost volatile state.

sources.supports: Preserved instance identity, addresses and EBS volumes, with lost RAM state
System status check metric, configurable alarms, notifications and recovery prerequisites

editorial_notes: Preserved answer 4. Added the existing auto-assigned public IPv4 constraint to distinguish recovery from an otherwise automatable Elastic IP and stop/start design.
